daily_brief: Global oil markets surged past $100 per barrel on Wednesday following escalating US-Iran strikes and continued Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities [BBC], marking the first breach of that threshold since July when a US-Iran ceasefire collapsed. In a significant diplomatic development, twelve Western nations including Britain, France, and Canada announced coordinated sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank [RFI, Al Jazeera], prompting Israeli retaliation against the UK [Le Monde]. The US-Canada trade war intensified as President Trump announced new import bans on Canadian alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles following Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs [BBC]. Meanwhile, France hosted a major international space summit in Paris that was notably snubbed by US companies SpaceX and Blue Origin, reportedly due to political pressure [RFI, France 24], underscoring growing transatlantic technology tensions. The 2025 PISA education results released this week revealed continued declines in student performance globally, with French scores hitting record lows [RFI] and concerns mounting about teenage academic achievement [The Economist]. In AI developments, an Anthropic researcher quit warning that developers 'earnestly believe' AI could be catastrophic [ABC Australia], while OpenAI claimed a mathematical breakthrough that sparked controversy over research credit [France 24].

top_stories.headline: Oil Surges Past $100 as US-Iran Strikes Escalate and Houthis Target Saudi Facilities
bullets: Brent crude rose above $100 per barrel for the first time since July, when a US-Iran ceasefire collapsed
The US struck five Iranian tankers, including four in the Gulf of Oman linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps and one near Kharg Island
Iran responded by launching missiles at a US base in Jordan and claiming attacks on two US vessels and eight oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
Houthi forces continued attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities, and Red Sea tankers following the breakdown of their informal ceasefire with Riyadh in July

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on price impact and detailed chronology of strikes

top_stories.headline: Twelve Western Nations Announce Coordinated Sanctions on Israeli Settlement Trade
bullets: Britain, Canada, France, and nine other countries announced plans to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank
The joint statement cited 'unprecedented levels of settler violence and settlement expansion' undermining prospects for a two-state solution
Israel announced retaliatory measures against the UK including banning 12 British MPs from entering Israel and closing the British consulate in Jerusalem
France has been pushing for EU-wide sanctions but has been blocked by some member states

top_stories.headline: US Escalates Trade War with New Bans on Canadian Alcohol, Dairy, and Motorcycles
bullets: President Trump signed executive orders banning imports of Canadian alcoholic spirits, some dairy goods, and motorcycles, effective September 29
The measures follow Canada's retaliatory tariffs on American goods coming into force
Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc called the measures 'unjustified' and promised to work 'in good faith' to resolve tensions
Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that Canada's pivot away from the US as its largest trading partner 'will come at a cost'

sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage of both sides' positions

top_stories.headline: Major US Space Companies Boycott Paris International Space Summit Amid Political Pressure
bullets: SpaceX, Blue Origin, and other US startups declined to attend France's International Space Summit, with French officials citing political pressure
Around 2,000 participants from 120 countries are attending the two-day event at the Grand Palais, co-hosted by France and Germany
Russia, Iran, and North Korea are absent, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cited scheduling conflicts for not attending
The summit aims to produce agreements on space traffic management and scientific data sharing as Europe seeks to strengthen its position against US and Chinese dominance

sources.framing_note: Detailed reporting on US company absences and ministry confirmation of political pressure

top_stories.headline: Global Student Performance Continues Decline in 2025 PISA Results
bullets: The 2025 PISA survey assessed 760,000 students across 91 countries, with science as the major focus area
French students recorded their lowest-ever scores, with reading comprehension dropping 18 points and mathematics dropping 16 points from 2022
New Zealand ranked 9th in reading, 10th-equal in science, and 14th-equal in mathematics, though officials noted sampling may have skewed results upward
French Education Minister blamed social media as one cause and pledged to focus on middle school standards
